notes.meaning: Christian slaves are told to show deep respect to their masters. Paul explains that if they rebel or act disrespectfully, people will speak evil of God and the Christian faith. Faithful, honest work protects the honor of the gospel in the eyes of outsiders.

Slaves who have Christian masters must not look down on them or become careless just because they are spiritual equals. Instead, they should work even harder because the person benefiting from their labor is a dearly loved brother in Christ. Timothy is charged to teach these standards clearly to the church.

Paul warns against anyone who promotes ideas that differ from the healthy teachings of the Lord Jesus Christ. True Christian teaching always leads to godliness, which means living a life that pleases God. Any message that strays from Christ's words damages the spiritual health of believers.

A teacher who opposes sound doctrine is full of pride and really understands nothing. Such a person has a sick craving for arguments and hair-splitting debates over words. These useless fights only produce jealousy, anger, insults, and cruel suspicions.

These debates create constant friction among people whose thinking has been ruined and who have lost grip on the truth. Such false teachers treat religion merely as a clever way to make money. Timothy must turn away from people who misuse faith for earthly profit.

True godliness really is a source of great wealth when it is joined with contentment. Contentment means resting satisfied with what God gives rather than hungering for more worldly goods. A quiet, satisfied heart brings peace in this life and eternal blessing in the next.

Humans enter the world completely empty-handed, and no one can take earthly possessions past the grave. Realizing that money stays behind helps keep our present desires in proper balance. Remembering our frail beginning and end frees us from greedy anxiety.

If believers have the basic necessities of life, such as food, clothing, and shelter, they should be fully satisfied. God promises to provide what His children truly need each day. Gratefulness for simple provisions protects the heart from restless greed.

People who fix their hearts on becoming wealthy walk straight into a dangerous trap. That craving stirs up foolish and harmful desires that pull a person down into misery. Chasing after riches at all costs can ultimately drown both body and soul in eternal ruin.

The love of money, rather than money itself, is a fertile source of all kinds of wrongdoing. Driven by this craving, some people have drifted away from true faith in Christ. In the end, their greed brings sharp pangs of regret and deep sorrow to their own souls.

differ.view: Some read it as "the root of all evils." They say the love of money means wanting what money buys instead of God, so it truly lies behind every evil.

notes.meaning: Paul calls Timothy a man of God, urging him to run far away from the lure of greed. Instead of seeking wealth, he must run hard after righteousness, faith, love, patience, and a gentle spirit. True spiritual leaders focus their energy on godly character rather than earthly treasures.

Timothy must actively fight the good fight of faith, just like an athlete competing for a prize. He is told to take firm hold of eternal life, which God called him to possess. Paul reminds him of the bold public confession of faith he made before many witnesses.

differ.view: Baptist teachers see the good confession as the public confession Timothy made at his baptism.
The "many witnesses" point to Timothy's ordination, when he was set apart for ministry.
Methodist teachers have suggested his baptism, or a time when he stood firm while imprisoned for Christ.

notes.meaning: Paul gives Timothy a solemn charge in the sight of God, who gives and preserves all life. He also charges him before Christ Jesus, who bravely declared the truth during His trial before Governor Pontius Pilate. Looking to Christ's courage under pressure inspires believers to remain faithful.

Timothy must guard the gospel and obey God's commands without any moral stain or fault. He is to keep this high standard faithfully until the visible return of the Lord Jesus Christ. Anticipating Christ's appearing motivates believers to live pure and blameless lives today.

God will reveal Christ's return at the exact time He has appointed in His perfect wisdom. The verse praises God as the blessed and only Ruler, the supreme King over all earthly kings and Lord over all lords. No human ruler compares to His ultimate power and sovereignty.

God alone possesses deathless life in His very nature, living in brilliant light that no creature can approach. No human being has ever seen Him or can see Him with physical eyes. To this glorious and majestic God belong everlasting honor and supreme rule.

Timothy must tell wealthy believers not to become proud or put their trust in riches, which can vanish in a moment. Instead, their hope belongs solely in the living God, who generously supplies good things for His people to enjoy. Real security comes from the Giver, not the gifts.

The wealthy are commanded to use their resources to do good and become rich in noble deeds. They should hold their possessions loosely, giving freely and gladly sharing with those in need. Generosity turns material abundance into a practical blessing for others.

By practicing open-handed generosity, believers build a solid foundation of heavenly treasure for the future. Sharing what they have now helps them lay hold of what is truly and genuinely life. Using wealth for God's purposes prepares the soul for everlasting joy.

Paul makes a passionate final appeal, telling Timothy to guard the true gospel like a valuable deposit left in his care. He must turn away from godless, meaningless talk and the conflicting arguments of false teachings that pretend to be deep knowledge. Protecting the purity of God's truth is a vital pastoral duty.

Some people who chased after this falsely called knowledge ended up wandering completely away from the Christian faith. Paul closes his letter by praying that God's undeserved favor and help will remain with Timothy and the entire church. Staying grounded in God's grace keeps believers safe from spiritual ruin.
